behaviors.feature: /name attaches a skill to one message
behaviors.cursor: Every /name at the start or after whitespace that names a skill attaches it to the submitted message, each once (findSkillReferences, regex (?:^|\s)/([a-zA-Z0-9_-]+)); interactive and headless submit paths both use it.
behaviors.pi: input handler: the first referenced skill rides Pi's /skill:name expansion; each further skill is a skill block ahead of the message; the message text is kept.
behaviors.changedThisRun: Before this run only a leading /name attached a skill.
behaviors.difference: A message that starts with a user's own prompt template keeps only the template: Pi expands templates after input handlers and exports no expander, so skills named later in that message are not attached. pstack ships no prompt templates.

behaviors.feature: Skill as a sticky Custom Mode

behaviors.pi: /mode <skill> [task], /mode off, /mode. Same notice texts; the skill block rides the system prompt on every request; badge in the footer.
evidence: docs: docs_skills.md Using a skill as a Custom Mode

behaviors.difference: The trigger is /mode instead of Option+Enter, and the skill sits in a system-prompt section instead of the entering user message. The model sees the same text.

behaviors.feature: Subagent types: built-ins and plugin agents
behaviors.cursor: Agent files parse name, description, model (default inherit), readonly, is_background/background, tools, force-default-model. Built-in explore uses a faster model by default. The CLI enum also has shell, browser-use, computer-use and others; an earlier capture of CLI 2026.10.01 listed generalPurpose, explore, cursor-guide, ci-investigator, bugbot, security-review, best-of-n-runner plus plugin agents.
behaviors.pi: generalPurpose and explore built-ins plus the four shipped agent files (name, description, model, readonly, is_background). explore defaults to the fast variant of the parent model.
behaviors.difference: Cursor-internal types that pstack never names (cursor-guide, ci-investigator, bugbot, security-review, best-of-n-runner, browser) are not offered. team-kit's thermo-nuclear agent mentions subagent_type shell, which the observed CLI also does not list; a Task with shell fails in both.

behaviors.cursor: Foreground returns the final text; background returns at once and enqueues a completion (title = first prompt line, 80 chars) that wakes the parent after its turn. Background runs are detached from the turn's abort signal.
behaviors.pi: One pi --mode rpc child per agent; background children are not tied to the turn signal; completion arrives as a pstack/task notification after the turn.

behaviors.cursor: CLI: resume of a finished agent continues it; resume while it runs fails with 'Sub-agent is currently running...'; lineage must match. pstack text describes steering a running agent, which the CLI does not do.
behaviors.pi: Resume continues a finished agent; resume of a running agent steers the prompt into its run (pstack's described behavior); lineage is checked by workspace records.
behaviors.difference: Follows pstack's described steer instead of the CLI's refusal.

behaviors.cursor: readonly sends the child prompt in ASK mode and restricts its resources (5622.index.js executeSubagentOnce); docs: no file edits, no state-changing shell commands; strips MCP.

behaviors.cursor: A cloud subagent runs on its own VM and branch, keeps running with the laptop closed, uses team MCP configuration (docs_subagents.md Cloud subagents).

behaviors.difference: No remote VM, no laptop-off execution, no team MCP configuration. Pi has no hosted agent runtime.
